source_excerpt: and never emits a host part (a path starting `//` gets an explicit empty authority; a Windows drive path takes the `file:///C:/...` form). The runner and preflight open the database through the shared `connect_sqlite(path, read_only=...)`, and both take the path from `sqlite_path_from_url` (three slashes relative, four absolute; rejects query parameters and a host/user/password/port). Because `mode=ro` never creates a file, with `read_only = true` the `sqllens serve` startup check (`_probe_sqlite` in [src/sqllens/preflight.py](../../../src/sqllens/preflight.py)) opens the file read-only, reads `PRAGMA schema_version`, and fails naming the path (and its resolved absolute form) when the file is missing or is not a SQLite database. With `read_only = false` the open is plain and creates a missing file.

With ``read_only`` the open goes through the ``mode=ro`` URI, so a missing
    file fails here instead of being created, and the schema header is read so
    a directory or a non-empty non-database file fails too (a zero-byte file
    opens as an empty database). A URL the helper rejects is reported with the
    helper's own message; a driver error names the path (a SQLite path carries
    no credentials) and the exception type, never the driver's ``str(exc)``.
